source.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization Leads to Low-Rank Features
source.authors: Maksym Andriushchenko; Dara Bahri; H. Mobahi; Nicolas Flammarion

record.tranche_reason: The study's own MS-COCO bottleneck experiment tests whether directly inducing low-rank features improves generalization and reports mixed retrieval outcomes; other findings concern feature rank and generalization jointly but do not test the catalog versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper measures feature rank and test or retrieval error while varying SAM strength, but the claim versions concern random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected models, optimizer comparisons, batch-size penalties, dropout, sharpness measures, and removing memorized examples. Those version-specific interventions are not tested here. Figure-only curves are not assigned reconstructed numeric values.
record.test_reason: Figure 11 reports CIFAR-10 test-error curves at batch sizes 512 and 1024 under the same 200-epoch budgets and training settings used for batch size 256 in Figure 1. These results bear on V5, although the supplied text does not reveal the cross-batch error differences. The main SAM, feature-rank, and bottleneck experiments do not test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate. SAM broadly reduces feature rank, with an explicit MLP-Mixer exception, and suitable radii improve generalization. Direct bottlenecks give only a marginal imagewise improvement and worsen textwise retrieval. The authors regard low rank as a useful side effect and leave the source of SAM's natural-data generalization gains unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study focuses on SAM, a perturbed-gradient training method, and compares it with standard training and direct linear bottlenecks; it does not reproduce the interventions or measures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: SAM ρ changes feature rank monotonically in many settings, while test/retrieval error improvement is U-shaped or mixed; augmentation is important for revealing the rank trend in the CIFAR experiments; feature-rank direction has an exception in MLP-Mixers after 3/4 blocks; attention/MLP subblock and architecture affect the observed low-rank mechanism.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM generally lowers feature rank and improves held-out performance at suitable perturbation radii; excessively large radii can hurt performance despite further rank reduction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM induces a low-rank feature bias whose strength does not monotonically predict held-out performance.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM prunes ReLU activations in some networks, while the ViT results implicate attention blocks without decreasing active GeLUs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The mechanism producing SAM's low-rank features depends on architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Bottlenecks change imagewise retrieval error from 23.3% to 22.7% and textwise error from 22.2% to 22.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directly enforcing low-rank final features does not consistently improve MS-COCO retrieval.

record.problems: Many central error/rank curves are presented only as figures, without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. ImageNet-1k model checkpoints use training details from cited papers. The study does not test the listed claim versions' central interventions; the teacher-student result uses SAM for only half of training and a special PCA threshold. The ImageNet table extraction has a flattened/duplicated column heading for one model, limiting exact attribution.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows omitted; figure-only curves were retained only where the text describes the trend. Detailed per-block ViT rank curves and auxiliary feature-rank-threshold/batch-size plots are not separately rowed because they do not report outcomes on the claim versions and their values are figure-only.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label versus random-label performance.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and local-connectivity interventions.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets and recovery interventions.
Longer-training and recipe-adaptation remedies are not tested as batch-size remedies. Cross-batch test-error differences in Figures 1 and 11 cannot be read from the supplied text.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and comparisons against norm- or margin-based predictors. SAM optimization is not that measurement.
Removal of memorized examples versus equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T5 rationale concerns a low-rank hypothesis outside V1–V8. Figure 11 nevertheless includes held-out test error, not just feature rank, under varied batch sizes and fixed epoch budgets, making it relevant to V5. Its omission is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not listed as missing. No V5 verdict is justified without readable cross-batch outcomes. All existing rows retain versions ["none"]; their states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not denials of the paper's reported SAM effects.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label generalization comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No large-batch generalization-gap test; batch size is varied only in supplementary feature-rank experiments.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measure or comparison of generalization-gap predictors.

rows.subject: PreAct ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 while varying SAM perturbation radius ρ; report test error and intermediate-block feature rank.

conditions.value: minimal: small learning rate, no momentum, no weight decay

rows.measure: Test error and intermediate-block feature rank (99% PCA variance)
rows.value: SAM improves test error over some ρ values; feature rank decreases monotonically with ρ. Numeric values are figure only.
rows.note: Authors describe the error improvement as U-shaped in ρ and the feature-rank reduction as monotonic; no curve values transcribed.
rows.check: Reports effects of SAM radius, not a cross-batch comparison. It supplies the batch-256 setting relevant to comparison with Figure 11.

rows.subject: R+Ti/16 vision transformer and BERT encoders
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on MS-COCO
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune image and text encoders with InfoNCE contrastive loss while varying SAM ρ.
rows.measure: Imagewise and textwise retrieval error; image and text feature rank
rows.value: SAM substantially improves retrieval error and reduces feature rank; numeric values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper reports an aggregate image-text training finding; separate image and text curves are not numerically reconstructed.
rows.check: SAM versus standard Adam is not an adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison. Split retrieval errors and feature ranks by encoder or retrieval direction.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU student network
rows.size_stated: m = 100 student neurons; d = 3 input dimension
rows.stage_stated: trained on teacher-student regression task; SAM used for first 50% of iterations, then disabled for convergence
rows.operation_detail: Vary SAM ρ and measure test loss, feature rank, active ReLUs, and weight norm.
rows.measure: Test loss, feature rank, number of active ReLUs, ℓ2 weight norm
rows.value: At ρ = 0.6, feature rank is 4 instead of 19; 10 out of 100 neurons are activated on at least one training example.
rows.note: Authors state that higher ρ generalizes better in this setup; SAM is disabled after the first half of iterations to achieve full convergence.
rows.check: Fixed-width teacher-student regression with varying SAM radius does not test widening beyond interpolation or any other listed version.

rows.subject: Post-activation ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch
rows.operation_detail: Vary SAM ρ and measure intermediate block rank and active ReLUs.

conditions.value: minimal: small step sizes, no momentum, no weight decay
at least 5% of maximum value on any training example

rows.measure: Feature rank and proportion of active ReLUs by residual block
rows.value: Both measures tend to decrease with ρ, particularly at later blocks; at ρ = 0.6 block 4 has 77% active ReLUs versus 100% for standard training.
rows.note: Authors say this directly contributes to lower rank but is not the only mechanism.
rows.check: Activation sparsity and feature rank do not measure a listed version.

rows.subject: ViT image encoder
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on MS-COCO
rows.operation_detail: Measure changes in feature rank across attention and MLP subblocks and count active GeLUs while varying SAM ρ.
rows.measure: Rank changes across subblocks; active GeLUs
rows.value: Attention blocks increase rank less at higher ρ; MLP blocks vary; no decrease in active GeLUs over ρ.
rows.note: The paper attributes rank reduction primarily to attention blocks in this setting and reports no coordinate-aligned sparsity in the residual stream.
rows.check: Attention-block rank changes and GeLU activity do not measure a listed version.

rows.subject: MS-COCO image and text encoders with linear bottleneck layers
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on MS-COCO
rows.operation_detail: Vary bottleneck inner dimension to induce low-rank features and measure imagewise and textwise retrieval error.
rows.note: The paper says low-rank features alone do not consistently enhance generalization: imagewise error marginally improves while textwise error worsens.
rows.check: Direct bottlenecks and retrieval performance test a separate low-rank hypothesis. Split imagewise and textwise outcomes; the text does not assign the quoted errors to a particular bottleneck dimension.
